title: SP3: the positional playbook. For every liquid stock (and the two indices) each evening: which entry, which exit and holding time (2-60 sessions) suits today's situation, or no trade
why: the evidence points to positional first: a 5-60 session trade pays about 0.3-0.5% round trip (at Rs 12,000-50,000 a position) against moves of 2-10%, intraday pays about 0.15% against 0.3-0.5% (audit 19 Oct, section 5)

what we learned is about timing and context, not stock picking: saturation (E04) and oversold (P01) pass false-discovery control but fail the within-day shuffle; weak markets paid more (E08, C07, C09 OPPOSITE; C06 FII long OPPOSITE); holding beat clever exits (E02, E06, E09, E11) and time/structure exits led (G01). SP3 turns these from single filters into one situation-dependent policy, as SP1 did for the index intraday

Madhav's rule, from the crypto lab: gather everything first (the unfiltered baseline book), then filter and tune only by findings measured against that baseline, station by station (the car-manufacturing line: raw material, assembly, quality check, repair shop, road test)

evidence_status.seen: 2018-2023 has been seen by the E/C/P/V studies on overlapping entry sets: every SP3 validation row is labelled SEEN and scored with registry rule seen_val_only; nothing on 2018-2023 can confirm
evidence_status.family_bar: SP3 rows are recorded in family SP3, but the bar for every seen and exploratory row is the Bonferroni z over bar_families (fixed now): exit, stop, gate, reposition, staging, indicator, portfolio, context, context_events, filter, events (V01-V03, whose band findings shaped BAND), flows (C06, which shaped the FII feature) and SP3 itself; k is PINNED at the freeze so it cannot drift as rows are recorded: 728 distinct (study, variant) rows in those families on 20 Oct 2026 plus SP3's 14 dev/validation rows (9 seen, 5 exploratory) = 742, z = 3.985, written to each row (review_2 should-fix 6; recount at the freeze if the ledger has grown). registry.register(..., bar_families=[...], union_k=742, holdout_k=7) stores them on the registration line, and registry.record uses union_k for rules seen_val_only and standard, holdout_k for rule holdout_one_sided (B8)
evidence_status.confirmatory: only the registered SP3 holdout run (tests.holdout), opened once after Madhav approves the frozen policy
evidence_status.untouched_by_sp3: no SP3 code has read 2024+ rows; the live stock paper engine reads the last 460 days through the logged paper_lookback purpose (observation, never scoring)
evidence_status.prior_openings_disclosed: the completed sp1_holdout run opened cm_bhavcopy, kite_index (day and minute), kite_5m, flows, fo_bhavcopy and fo_greeks for 2024-01-01 to 2026-10-16; it computed index intraday rules and the SP1 breadth input (the share of top names above their open), never any stock's positional performance. The live paper engine's 460-day lookback shows recent prices to the paper journal, not outcomes of SP3 actions. Recorded so the holdout's freshness is judged honestly

data.prices: gold/bars/adj_daily (adjusted with the corporate-action factors, applied only when both records agree or the price confirms; the 75 ambiguous events stay flagged), the daily features table gold/features/daily.parquet and gold/universe/u_liq_in.parquet, all to 2023-12-29 (lab rebuilt 19 Oct with the 30 weekend sessions). Entry signals and features use series EQ bars, as the lab builds them. HOLDING-WINDOW bars use the stock's EQ, BE and BZ rows from silver cm_bhavcopy (review_2 blocker 2, review_3 blocker 1): for every holding row, cum_factor = the product of the applied factors in silver/corporate_actions/factors.parquet for that row's symbol with an ex-date after the row's date (the catalog formula, computed on all series, since the factors are keyed by symbol and ex-date and catalog.cm_adj is EQ-only); one row is kept per (sid, date), the highest-turnover series; a move between series is neither a halt nor a stop. Rupee result of a trade = shares x raw entry fill x (adjusted exit fill / adjusted entry fill), so an applied split inside a window is not a loss. A symbol change is followed to the successor symbol (from 2011 the ISIN entity does this; before 2011 from the permanent-stop list's 'renamed' class). sid is the entity string as stored in gold/features (the ISIN entity from 2011, the symbol before)
data.index_futures: silver/fo_bhavcopy FUTIDX rows for NIFTY (from 2000) and BANKNIFTY (from 2005), daily OHLC per contract, with silver/fo_calendar for expiries (B7)
data.context: silver/kite_index (Nifty 50, Nifty Bank, India VIX, Smallcap 100, Nifty 100, daily from 2003), silver/us/us_close (QQQ from Tiingo, 2003+), participant OI (2012+), delivery (2003+), the event registry (scheduled calendar rows only, scenario.scheduled_dates), board-meeting intimations and results filings with their broadcast times (silver/pr, results index), price-band hits (silver/pr), stock-futures membership (silver/fo_bhavcopy FUTSTK rows on the day)
data.coverage_rule: a feature or a family enters SP3 only if its source covers the whole holdout window: coverage = the sessions with a source file between 2024-01-01 and 2026-09-30, presence only (no row counts, which would leak market state, e.g. band hits per month); a source passes with files on at least 99% of sessions and no gap longer than 5 sessions; checked before the freeze through sealed.coverage(manifest), which reads only the download manifests (manifests/<dataset>.jsonl: status 200 by date, window or year) and no data file, sealed or not (logged under purpose coverage); for windowed queries every session inside a window with a status-200 manifest entry counts as present; downloader logs for sealed dates print presence only. For event sources that do not produce one file per session (results, announcements, board meetings), presence = a download-manifest entry with status 200 for that session's date query. The 2025+ results API replaces the old results index, so the check also confirms that the broadcast time means the same thing on dates both sources cover: sample = the lowest 200 of hash(filing_id, 19) among 2018-2023 filings present in both sources; pass if at least 190 match to the minute (review_2 should-fix 3, review_3 should-fix 4). Known gaps on 20 Oct: PR zips (band hits, board meetings) to Oct 2025 and the results index to 2024, so before the freeze the downloaders extend them to 2026-09-30 into sealed/ (written, not read); whatever still falls short at the freeze is dropped from the policy everywhere (dev, validation and holdout) and reported descriptively only, listed in the frozen file (should-fix 1)
data.not_used: FRED USD/INR and Brent (published days late: not known at the decision time); GDELT (that channel is EVC's); fundamentals (V05's, still downloading); the sector map (today's Nifty 500 list is not point in time, so a 'missing' sector means 'did not survive into today's index': descriptive only, on covered names, never a model feature, B2)
data.periods: walk-forward test years 2010-2017 reported as dev (not gating), 2018-2023 validation (SEEN), training from 2005; holdout 2024-01-01 to 2026-09-30 (sealed, fixed now)

decision_point.when: after the close of session T (the live engine decides 22:30 Toronto, before T+1 opens); every input is known by then: closes of T, delivery of T, participant OI of T (published the evening of T), the last US close dated before the entry session T+1 (the US session of date T, on Tiingo by 17:30 New York), filings broadcast before T+1 09:00 IST
decision_point.fill: stocks: T+1 official open plus the half-spread for the stock's turnover rank (costs.py estimate); no further slippage is added (the costs-and-spreads x2 robustness row covers it); exits as the harness fills them (close-based exits at the next open; stops and targets in the bar at the level, or at the open if it gaps through). Index: the near-month future's T+1 open plus 1 tick, exits plus 1 tick

universe.stocks: liquidity rank 1-250 by 60-session median turnover on T (U_LIQ-IN rule: series EQ, close above Rs 10, no ETFs or funds, at least 126 sessions); eligibility uses data dated T or earlier only: a stock with an unconfirmed corporate-action flag in the 200 sessions up to and including T is not a candidate that day (B1)
universe.index: NIFTY 50 and NIFTY BANK, traded through the near-month future (index_futures)

in_window_events.rule: an event after T never removes a trade (B1). Every case below is counted by family and year, and listed before any outcome is read
in_window_events.ca_artifact: an unconfirmed corporate action inside the holding window: the trade closes at the close before it (reason ca_artifact). A one-day move above 50% is ca_artifact only when an unconfirmed corporate-action flag, or a split, bonus or consolidation record, lies within 5 sessions of it; any other move is real and is taken (Yes Bank, 6 Mar 2020, is a real move), and a stop fills at the open if the price gaps through it (review_2 blocker 1)
in_window_events.halt: a gap of more than 10 calendar days between the stock's sessions (EQ, BE and BZ rows together): the trade exits at the first open after trading resumes (reason halt)
in_window_events.boundary: E = the period end (2023-12-29 for dev and validation; 2026-09-30 in the holdout run); L = the stock's last session (any of EQ, BE, BZ, following renames) on or before E. If E - L is at least 62 market sessions, the stock is a permanent stop; otherwise its open positions at the end are data_end (review_3 should-fix 1)
in_window_events.permanent_stop: classes, for 2005-2023 from pre_freeze.permanent_stops (registrations/sp3_permanent_stops.csv, frozen): scheme of arrangement or amalgamation, and voluntary delisting: the position closes at L's close with no exit fees (reason end_scheme); renamed: followed to the successor sid, not a stop; compulsory delisting, liquidation, suspension without resumption (including a suspension still unresolved at E) and unresolved: -100% (reason end_failed). The slot frees at the session after L. The sensitivity marks every case at L's close (review_2 blocker 2, review_3 blocker 2)
in_window_events.holdout_permanent_stops: stocks that stop in 2024-2026 are classified inside the sp3_holdout run by a MECHANICAL rule, with no manual lookup: scheme = an announcement or corporate-action record in an amalgamation, merger or scheme-of-arrangement category for the sid within the 250 sessions before L; voluntary_delisting = a delisting-offer or voluntary-delisting record in that window; renamed = the ISIN entity has sessions after L (followed, not a stop); otherwise end_failed (-100%) in the primary run and at L's close in the sensitivity. Before the freeze the same rule is run on 2005-2023 and its agreement with registrations/sp3_permanent_stops.csv is reported by class (review_3 blocker 2, review_4 item 2)
in_window_events.data_end: a stock with L within 62 market sessions of E, or a window that runs past E: open positions are marked at the last close with no exit fees (reason data_end), never read past the boundary; trade-level rows include only candidates signalled at least 62 market sessions before E (review_2 should-fix 7)
in_window_events.counting: the counts of ca_artifact, halt, permanent-stop and data_end cases listed before any outcome is read are counted per 61-bar candidate window, not per action (per-action counting would need exits) (review_3 should-fix 6)

stage_1_gather_everything.principle: the raw material: every candidate any of our entry families produces, unfiltered and uncapped, plus controls; nothing is dropped for being unpromising. More families add models, not test rows, so they cost nothing on the bar

families.BRK: 20-day high close on volume at least 1.5x its 20-day average, above the 200-day average (E02's BRK)
families.PULL: above the 200-day and at least 5% under the 20-day average (E02's PULL)
families.REV: RSI(14) under 30 (P01; the live paper engine's REV)
families.DECL: down more than 30% in 60 sessions (saturation after a decline, M-13; E04's decline flag)
families.BAND: a lower price-band hit within the last 5 sessions (V02/E11), as an entry family to measure (not to favour); subject to the coverage rule
families.HI52: T's close strictly above each of the previous 250 closes, above the 200-day average
families.LO52: T's close strictly below each of the previous 250 closes (measured long, like DECL)
families.SQZ: 20-day Bollinger width (4 x 20-day standard deviation / 20-day average) at T at or below the 10th percentile of the 250 widths ending at T, close above the 50-day average
families.BBMR: close under the lower Bollinger band (20 sessions, 2 standard deviations), above the 200-day average
families.GAPU: T's open at least 3% above T-1's close and T's close still at least 3% above T-1's close
families.GAPD: T's open at least 3% below T-1's close and T's close still at least 3% below T-1's close; T is not the ex-date of a dividend of 2% or more of T-1's close (price-only bars show those as false gaps); dividend records come from the PR zips, 2010 onward only, so GAPD starts in 2010, as BAND does (review_3 should-fix 5)
families.RESU: the company's first results broadcast of the quarter, broadcast after T-3's close and by T's close (15:30 IST), with T's close above the pre-broadcast close by more than 1 ATR(14) (ATR as of the pre-broadcast session); subject to the coverage rule
families.RESD: the same, below by more than 1 ATR(14); subject to the coverage rule
families.RETEST: the most recent day the BRK rule fired for the stock within the top 500 (the features table's coverage; whatever its liquidity rank within it or spacing that day), 5-60 sessions before T; level = the highest close of the 20 sessions before that day; T's low at or below level + 1 ATR(14) (ATR as of T) and T's close above the level
families.MOM: on the last session of each month: top decile, within the liquid 250, of c(T-20) / c(T-250) - 1 (the 250-session return skipping the last 20 sessions)
families.ANY: every liquid stock-day with hash(sid, date, 11) under the ANY rate (pre_freeze.candidate_counts), then the 14-day spacing (the no-entry-skill baseline; hash(sid, date, s) = the first 8 hex digits of sha256 of 'sid|YYYY-MM-DD|s' read as an integer and divided by 16^8, so the live engine reproduces it exactly)
families.CTL: for each day, as many liquid stocks as there are distinct real-family stock-days that day after spacing, taken in ascending hash(sid, date, 13) order; not spaced; the matched control, never chosen by the policy

stage_1_gather_everything.priority: one fixed order, chosen before any outcome is seen, decides which family's row a stock-day uses when it is in several (should-fix 5): RETEST, BRK, HI52, SQZ, MOM, GAPU, RESU, PULL, BBMR, REV, RESD, GAPD, BAND, DECL, LO52, ANY; a sensitivity reports the reverse order. Order of operations: spacing first within each family, then priority. Each family's model is fitted on its PRIORITY rows only (the population it is applied to); all rows stay in the candidate table for reports (review_2 should-fix 1)
stage_1_gather_everything.spacing: one candidate per stock per family per 14 calendar days (the lab rule), applied before priority
stage_1_gather_everything.index: every session for NIFTY and NIFTY BANK is a candidate (long and short)
stage_1_gather_everything.size_check: counts by family and year computed before the freeze (pre_freeze.candidate_counts, no outcomes). ANY rate = min(3%, (400,000 - non-ANY rows) / ANY-eligible rows), where non-ANY rows = all rows of every other family including CTL, after spacing and before priority, and ANY-eligible = eligible liquid stock-days 2005-2023 (review_3 should-fix 3), rounded down to 0.5%, at least 0.5%, written into this file as any_rate before the freeze, so the live engine's rules v1.3 use the same number. If the non-ANY rows alone exceed 400,000, no family is dropped and nothing is thinned: the run takes longer

stage_2_every_action.stock_exits: 26 actions + NO TRADE, each with the harness's 2 ATR(14) initial stop unless named otherwise: the 18 exit-harness policies exactly as the live paper engine runs them (exitlab.DEFAULT_POLICIES: hold 5/10/20/40/60 sessions; targets 1R/2R/3R; ATR trails 2/3/4; close below the 10/20/50-day average; swing lows 5/10/20; half then trail 3); hold60_low20 (60-session hold with a close-below-20-day-low exit, G01's validation leader); hold_2d and hold_3d; hold_20d and hold_60d with no initial stop; hold_20d and hold_60d with a 3 ATR initial stop; and the harness's random-exit control (5 draws, never chosen)
stage_2_every_action.stock_direction: long only (Indian cash delivery cannot be shorted overnight); stock-futures shorts are a later shadow study
stage_2_every_action.index_actions: long or short x {hold 5, 10, 20 sessions; close below (long) / above (short) the 10-day average, capped at 60 sessions; a close beyond the 20-day low (long) / high (short) with a 20-session limit} = 10 actions + NO TRADE; no ATR stop on any index action (stated, B7). Positions roll at the close two sessions before expiry into the next month, paying both legs' dated fees plus 1 tick each; spot is used only where a contract row is missing (counted)
stage_2_every_action.outcomes: per candidate x action: GROSS return from the fill prices (half-spread included, fees not), fees at the slot's rupee size on the decision date added later (B4), R against the 2 ATR stop, sessions held, worst and best move, exit reason; computed by exitlab's simulation (one schema with the live paper engine) with the in_window_events rules

costs.model: costs.py v1.2, used by SP3 and everything after it (recorded studies keep their stamped code): dated delivery STT 0.075% each side to 2005-05-31, 0.1% to 2006-05-31, 0.125% to 2013-05-31, 0.1% after; intraday sell-side 0.015% / 0.02% / 0.025% on the same dates; futures sell-side 0.01% to 2005-05-31, 0.0133% to 2006-05-31, 0.017% to 2013-05-31, 0.01% to 2023-03-31, then the current schedule; exitlab is changed, before the run, to pass the trade's entry and exit dates (when, sell_when), not the year, so the 1 Oct 2024 exchange-charge change applies by date (should-fix 8)
costs.at_size: every position's fees (brokerage, STT, exchange, SEBI, stamp, GST, the DP charge on the sell) are computed at its rupee size on its dates: Rs 12,000 at K=5 / Rs 60,000; Rs 20,000 at K=10 / Rs 2 lakh; Rs 50,000 at K=20 / Rs 10 lakh

stage_3_situation.market: Nifty trend (above both / below both / mixed of its 50- and 200-day), breadth (share of the liquid 250 above the 200-day) in training terciles, India VIX tercile and above/below its 50-day, small caps against large caps (Smallcap 100 / Nifty 100 ratio vs its 50-day), Nifty 20-session return tercile, Nasdaq (QQQ) above/below its 200-day and the last US session's move bucket (+/-1%), FII index-futures long share tercile (2012+; 'missing' before), a scheduled RBI/Budget/election day in the next 5 sessions
stage_3_situation.stock: distance from the 50-day (under 0, 0-20%, over 20%: E04's saturation line), RSI(14) bucket (under 30, 30-70, over 70), 20-session return tercile, volume heat (above 1.5x), delivery share above 60%, own 20-day volatility (top fifth of the day or not), liquidity bucket (1-50, 51-150, 151-250), F&O member (a FUTSTK row in that day's fo_bhavcopy, B2), and, subject to the coverage rule: lower band hit in the last 5 sessions, results filed in the last 5 sessions, a results board meeting intimated (before the decision) for the next 10 sessions. One broadcast cut-off for every filing-based feature: broadcast by 08:00 IST of T+1 (22:30 Toronto falls between 08:00 and 09:00 IST as daylight saving changes); only the first results broadcast per company per quarter counts (review_2 should-fix 9). For each index model, trend and 20-session return are computed on its own index (Nifty for NIFTY, Nifty Bank for BANKNIFTY), breadth and the rest as above (review_2 should-fix 5)
stage_3_situation.levels: every feature has a 'missing' level; terciles are fitted on the training years of each fold only

stage_4_learning.model: for each (family, action): ridge regression of GROSS return on one-hot situation features (main effects; intercept unpenalised; target winsorised at training 1st/99th percentiles for fitting, then the training mean of (raw minus winsorised) added back to the intercept so the tails stay in the prediction, should-fix 7); lambda by purged leave-one-year-out within the training years from {1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000}; out-of-fold residual variance for the prediction's standard error (the SP1 sandwich)
stage_4_learning.predicted_net: predicted gross minus the round-trip fees at the slot's rupee size on the decision date, a buy and a sell both at slot size (B4)
stage_4_learning.minimum: a (family, action) is modelled in a fold only with at least 300 training candidates over 3 or more training years; otherwise that family is not traded in that fold (BAND has no data before 2010, so it starts late; should-fix 9)
stage_4_learning.walk_forward: expanding: test year y in 2010..2023; training = candidates whose signal date is at least 62 market sessions before y's first session (exitlab's window is bars T+1 to T+61, so every bar of every training label is dated before y), from 2005, the same set for every action. For fitting, a training trade halted past y's first session is valued at its last close before the halt. Sessions are counted on the trading calendar, not the stock's own bars. Inner leave-one-year-out folds for lambda and c drop candidates signalled in the 62 market sessions before the held-out year (purge) and in the 62 after it (embargo). Each inner-CV book starts empty on the held-out year's first session and is marked to market through its last (review_2 blocker 3, should-fix 8)
stage_4_learning.score: one score everywhere (should-fix 5): predicted net / the training mean of sessions held for that (family, action); an action qualifies only if predicted net > c x SE and > 0
stage_4_learning.policy: for each candidate (the priority family's row of each stock-day): among qualifying actions, the highest score (ties: the earlier action in stage_2's order); if none qualifies, NO TRADE; score ties between candidates are broken by ascending hash(sid, date, 17) (the intercept-only policy gives every candidate in a family the same score); the share of days with idle slots is reported, since ranking by net per session gives up per-trade return when slots do not bind (review_2 blocker 6b, should-fix 10); random_exit and CTL are never chosen; an ANY row never competes with a real-family row (a stock-day with any real-family row uses that row). c from {0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3, 4, 6, 10} (should-fix 6) by purged nested leave-one-year-out inside the training years (best mean book return of that K/capital row; ties to the larger c), calibrated separately for each K/capital row (B4); the same rules per index
stage_4_learning.learned_report: the largest coefficients per family (what Ananta learned about each situation), and which actions the policy chose by year

stage_5_book.slots: the stock book is slot-limited (per-trade means overstate what a book earns because signals cluster in bull runs, G01): K equal slots fixed at book_inr / K, no compounding in scored rows (K = 5 at Rs 60,000; also K = 10 at Rs 2 lakh and K = 20 at Rs 10 lakh). Each evening, free slots take the day's policy trades in order of score; a trade that finds no free slot is recorded as NO SLOT (counted, outcome kept). Shares = floor(slot / T's raw (unadjusted) close), fixed in the decision file before the open (quantity orders are placed before the price is known); 0 shares = NO_SIZE (counted); the rupee result is shares x raw entry fill x (adjusted exit fill / adjusted entry fill), as in data.prices. Idle cash earns 0. A stock already held is recorded as HELD: no add, no exit reset. A slot freed at the T+1 open can be refilled at that open, but a stock whose position exits at the T+1 open is not bought back at that open (B5, review_2 should-fix 4). Every book (policy, baseline, intercept-only, CTL, fixed_exit, inner-CV) starts empty and applies the same slot and survival rules (review_3 blocker 4)
stage_5_book.daily_return: the change in equity marked to market at each close, divided by book_inr (B5)
stage_5_book.survival: paper_config.json survival, in every book (policy, baseline, intercept-only, CTL, fixed_exit, inner-CV): the 5% day line is evaluated on closes; a breach closes every position at the next open and is logged; the 22% drawdown line is evaluated and logged; scored rows use the continuing path (on paper the book keeps running after a 22% line, cfg-2026-10-19c, Madhav: everything runs and is tracked); the paused path is reported beside it (review_2 blocker 6d)
stage_5_book.index_book: one position per index; no new entry while one is open (B5). Contract: the near-month future, except that when T+1 is on or after the roll session (two sessions before expiry, fo_calendar) the entry is in the next month's contract; closes and rolls use the bhavcopy CLOSE field, not SETTLE_PR; a missing contract row in the middle of a trade carries the previous close forward (counted) (review_2 should-fix 5). Scored as a SHADOW book in bps of one future's notional: Rs 60,000 cannot margin one Nifty lot, and a positional option version needs its own theta-aware design (nice-to-have 4)
stage_5_book.baseline: the unfiltered baseline book (B5, review_2 blocker 6a): the same slots, filled each day from all real-family candidates (the priority family's row per stock-day) in ascending hash(sid, date, s) order (same hash rule), one book for each s = 101..120; the baseline series is the mean of the 20 books' daily returns. Its fixed action, one action for all families, is the one with the best 20-seed mean daily book return on that fold's training set (the policy's training candidates and years), refitted each test year like the policy
stage_5_book.fixed_exit_book: 'policy entries, fixed exit': the same K, the same gate (a candidate enters if any action qualifies for it) and the same score order as the policy, but every trade uses the baseline's fixed action for that test year (scored by STOCK|book|exit_choice)
stage_5_book.ctl_book: the same K and slot rules; each policy entry on day T, taken in the policy's score order, is shadowed by the next CTL candidate of T, in ascending hash(sid, date, 13) order, that the CTL book does not already hold, with the same action as the policy entry; a 'policy entry' is an entry that took a slot; a NO_SIZE CTL candidate is skipped for the next one in hash order; if the day's CTL list runs out the shadow is recorded as NO_CTL (counted); CTL draws only from eligible liquid stocks (the same corporate-action eligibility rule); no free CTL slot = NO SLOT (review_2 blocker 6c, review_3 should-fix 2)
stage_5_book.holdout_start: every holdout book starts empty on 2024-01-01 (review_2 blocker 6f)

stage_6_quality_check_and_tuning.against_the_baseline: at every station the same comparison: the policy book against (a) the unfiltered baseline book, (b) the same policy without situation features (intercept-only, same c rule), (c) CTL entries with the policy's chosen exits (entry skill), (d) Nifty buy-and-hold over the same days (exploratory: mostly beta, and price-only bars against the price index)
stage_6_quality_check_and_tuning.filters_as_findings: every named condition (conditions.py: saturation, market gate, VIX, breadth, small-cap lead, band hits...) is reported as on/off slices of the baseline book per family and action, dev and validation, descriptive; a filter is not hand-added to the policy: the policy's situation model already holds it as a feature. Whether a feature group earns its place is shown by drop-one ablations (nice-to-have 3), not by the policy beating intercept-only
reports: the book started in each of 12 different months (path dependence)
drop-one feature-group ablations: market trend, breadth, VIX, size, US, FII, scheduled events, stock technical, stock flow (volume, delivery), stock events (results, band)
liquidity halves (rank 1-125 and 126-250) run as separate books
slot use and the NO SLOT and NO_SIZE shares
dividends are not credited on price-only bars (stated)
stage_6_quality_check_and_tuning.tuning_budget: no tuning after the freeze; anything changed later (a new family, feature or exit) is sp3-v2 with its own rows, counted in the same bar

seen_rows: STOCK|book|vs_baseline: policy book minus the baseline book, per day, > 0
STOCK|book|vs_intercept_only: policy minus the same policy with no situation, per day, > 0
STOCK|book|vs_ctl: policy book minus CTL entries with the policy's chosen exits, per day, > 0 (entry skill)
STOCK|book|exit_choice: the policy book minus the fixed_exit_book (policy entries, the baseline's fixed action), per day, > 0 (exits are the priority; review_2 blocker 4)
INDEX|NIFTY|vs_intercept_only: policy minus intercept-only, per day, > 0
INDEX|BANKNIFTY|vs_intercept_only: policy minus intercept-only, per day, > 0
exploratory_rows: STOCK|trade|policy: per-trade net return of the policy's trades, quarter-block means
STOCK|book|vs_nifty: policy book minus Nifty buy-and-hold, per day
STOCK|trade|exit_choice: on each policy trade, the chosen action's net minus the baseline's fixed action's net on the same candidate, quarter-block means
tests.statistics: daily book rows: the verdict t is Newey-West with 5 lags on the marked-to-market daily series; a 20-session block bootstrap (2,000 draws, seed 17) is reported beside it and never decides (review_2 blocker 6e); trade rows: quarter-block means with the t over quarters (the lab's _blk convention), because neighbouring entries share most of their path. Fewer than 200 validation trades (stocks) or 100 validation trades per index = INCONCLUSIVE
tests.nulls: state-shuffle null, descriptive (its p-value cannot reach the bar): market-feature rows permuted across dates in month blocks, stock-feature vectors permuted within family and month, models refitted with lambda and c fixed at the real fit's values (as SP1 did), the whole policy and book rerun, 200 draws (seeds 1001-1200); reports the share of null books at or above the real one and how often the null trades
robustness: per test year (robust if at least 4 of 6 validation years positive)
permanent stops at the last close instead of -100%

holdout.window: 2024-01-01 to 2026-09-30, fixed now; it ends before paper started on 16 Oct 2026 (B6)
holdout.method: test years 2024, 2025 and 2026 (to 30 Sep) with the same annual expanding refit and c rule (training through the 62-market-session gap of stage_4_learning.walk_forward), costs in force on each date, the same book rules
holdout.rule: holdout_one_sided for every holdout row; the 5 above are labelled CONFIRMATORY, every other holdout row EXPLORATORY
holdout.minimums: at least 100 stock trades, and at least 40 trades per index, in the holdout; otherwise that row is INCONCLUSIVE (review_2 blocker 6f)
holdout.bar: PROPOSED, Madhav decides before the freeze: holdout_k = 7, FROZEN in this file: the rows on the sealed period labelled CONFIRMATORY (SP1's 2; SP1H recorded 5 rows under holdout_one_sided, 3 of them EXPLORATORY) plus SP3's 5. registry.record uses the registration's holdout_k for every SP3 holdout row, so the order of recording cannot change it; SP3's exploratory holdout rows are scored at the same z, labelled EXPLORATORY, and never counted in k (review_2 blocker 5). z = 2.69. Minimum detectable effect, on about 680 sessions: an annual Sharpe (or, for difference rows, information ratio) of about 1.64 for 50% power and about 2.15 for 80% power. The alternative is the union bar (k = 742, z = 3.985: about 2.4 for 50% power), under which NOT_CONFIRMED is all but certain. Dev and validation rows keep the union bar either way
holdout.access: through india/sealed.py as a new HOLDOUT_RUNS entry 'sp3_holdout' with end 2026-09-30 and its sealed folders fixed at the freeze: cm_bhavcopy, delivery, kite_index/day, flows, fo_bhavcopy, pr, announce (the 2024+ parts of each kept under sealed/silver). Not sealed, stated: us_close (not Indian market data), silver/corporate_actions, bronze/results_index and bronze/results_index_integrated (filings and corporate actions carry no prices; SP3's dev and validation code reads them only to 2023-12-29, checked by a date-filter test in the cross-check). The sp3_holdout run registers as its own study (as SP1H did), and its registry.register passes bar_families, union_k and holdout_k read from this frozen file (review_4 item C) (review_2 should-fix 11, review_4 item 3)

tests.scoring: seen rows: rule seen_val_only (2010-2017 reported as dev, not gating); exploratory rows recorded too (they count toward the bar)

paper.baseline_now: the live stock paper engine is already the baseline line (BRK, PULL, REV, CTL x the 18 exit policies, every candidate, since the 16 Oct decision). At the freeze it moves to rules v1.3: the SP3 families (DECL, BAND, HI52, LO52, SQZ, BBMR, GAPU, GAPD, RESU, RESD, RETEST, MOM, ANY by the hash rule, CTL by the hash rule) and the 8 added actions, still journaling every candidate. The SP3 baseline is then a filter over the live journal (rank at most 250, 14-day spacing, the CTL rule), so the live baseline and the research baseline are the same thing (should-fix 2)
paper.policy_later: after the holdout run and Madhav's approval: the frozen policy's decisions each evening (hash-chained ledger, written before the open), the K=5 Rs 60,000 book beside the unfiltered baseline, scored nightly; the baseline never stops
paper.promotion: a filter or the policy moves from paper to the main book only when history and the live record agree and Madhav approves

outputs: india/checks/sp3_crosscheck.py (independent bar-by-bar re-derivation of 300+ outcomes, the in_window_events cases and 20 book days before any result is read)
limits: the 5-minute data is not used (daily decisions); intraday entries are SP2's
results-intimation dates exist from the PR zips and the results index; a missing intimation is 'missing', never 'no results'
